comment: Hand-written. Families V01-V36 of docs/VANILLA_COMPLETION.md, their named mechanics, and the rules that assign every enumerated resource to a family. Statuses describe the source at the commit that changes this file; tools/compat_ledger.py validates it and generates compatibility/ledger.json and docs/VANILLA_LEDGER.md.

mechanics.name: Exact version manifests verified against the official artifacts
mechanics.note: compatibility/versions/; values read from the official jars, whose hashes match Mojang's published metadata

mechanics.name: Machine-readable feature and evidence ledger with validation
Reference traces of block state changes (circuit-trace v1)
Trace format with entity, lifecycle, inventory, dimension, ticket and RNG observations
mechanics.note: circuit-trace 2: Circuit records and evaluates it; the reference harness does not record it yet

mechanics.name: Reference harness recording v2 observations on both releases, with repeat runs
mechanics.note: Both releases; repeat runs on fresh worlds; the level random is seeded with 0

mechanics.name: Scenario adapters for official server, sequential, parallel and real-client runs with first-mismatch reports
mechanics.note: tools/scenario.py runs a skeleton sequentially, in parallel and on each harness, and reports the first difference of every pair (circuit-server --diff-fixtures)
deviations: real-client checks are separate scripts, not driven from skeletons

mechanics.name: Protocol-client scenarios compared between the official servers and Circuit
mechanics.note: External mineflayer scripts; outputs compared by diff

mechanics.name: Real-client step scripts against Circuit
mechanics.note: Checks Circuit with the unmodified client; not a comparison with the official server

mechanics.name: Internal representation of every block and state property
mechanics.note: circuit-blocks-1 from public data: 1,106 internal blocks and 27,958 internal states with stable ids; every state of both releases round-trips through notation and wire ids

mechanics.name: Per-version mapping between internal states and protocol state ids
mechanics.note: Every state of both releases maps to one Circuit state and back

mechanics.name: Collision shapes of block states
mechanics.note: Every state's collision boxes, from the block registry (minecraft-data), equal to both official servers' report; items and players move against them. Offsets some blocks apply by position are not modeled
deviations: position-dependent offsets (bamboo, pointed dripstone and others) are not applied

mechanics.name: Hardness, blast resistance, harvest tools, light emission and opacity, friction, sounds
mechanics.note: Hardness, effective tool and harvest tier of every block from public data, the tool and tier from the block tags when the official data pack is loaded; opacity from its light filtering

families.name: Item and entity components and registries

mechanics.name: Item stacks with count, stack size and damage
Other item components: names, lore, enchantments, attributes, potions, food, containers, books, maps, dyes, fireworks, trims and the rest
mechanics.note: Every component type of both protocols is read, checked against its registries and kept losslessly in canonical form (schema compiled from minecraft-data); 29 components have a save form for Anvil interchange
deviations: components that refer to registries the server does not synchronize (enchantments, trim materials and patterns, banner patterns, instruments, jukebox songs, data component predicates) are refused
the rules use only damage, max stack size and max damage, and for eating and drinking a potion's contents, a suspicious stew's effects and an ominous bottle's amplifier
a stack's components are written in type order; the official servers write a patch in the order its components were set (clients read it as a map; client/special_a)

mechanics.name: Component and entity-data schema changes of 1.21.5
mechanics.note: The 1.21.5 component schema (96 types, length-prefixed creative values) is read and written
deviations: entity-data schema changes are not modeled

mechanics.name: Hashed item stacks in container clicks (1.21.5 and later)
Entity data and components (variants, custom names, equipment)
Known-pack exchange and registry data by name
mechanics.note: Vanilla pack only

mechanics.name: Synchronized registries with data for clients without the vanilla pack
mechanics.note: Each bundle names its registry set: 17 registries for 1.21.8 and 11 for 1.21.4 sent by name to clients with the vanilla pack, the same entries as the official servers; clients without the pack get a documented minimal set with data
deviations: 1.21.8 dialogs and game-test registries are not sent
clients without the vanilla pack get only dimension types, plains and the chat type with data
enchantments are sent only with the official jar's data pack

mechanics.name: Tag synchronization and evaluation
mechanics.note: With the official jar's data pack: every tag of block, item, entity type, fluid and the synchronized registries, as many per registry as the official servers send; without it, the biome tags 1.21.4 needs
deviations: tags of game events, points of interest and 1.21.8 dialogs are not loaded
tags are not reloaded while the server runs

mechanics.name: Data-pack stack, selection, ordering and reload
mechanics.note: The official jar's built-in pack, then directories and archives in configured order; later files replace earlier ones, tag files merge; pack formats checked
deviations: no pack selection, filters, overlays or /reload
the experimental packs inside the jar are not loaded

mechanics.name: Experimental feature flags and built-in experimental packs
mechanics.note: minecart_improvements, redstone_experiments, trade_rebalance in both releases

mechanics.name: The overworld dimension
mechanics.note: Flat floor, plains

mechanics.name: The Nether, the End and custom dimensions with dimension-scoped state
mechanics.note: Every level keeps its own columns, scheduled ticks, block events, block entities, entities and per-level counters, and levels tick in the order overworld, Nether, End (minecraft.wiki "Tick"); entity ids are counted over all levels. Commands, tickets, traces, checkpoints, replays and logs name the level. Differential tests prove identical coordinates in two levels independent in the engine and the oracle
deviations: the Nether and the End are neither generated nor reachable by players
level-specific rules (ultrawarm water and lava, the Nether's roof, the End's void and dragon fight) are not modeled
custom dimensions from data packs are not supported

mechanics.name: Vanilla ticket types (player, forced, portal, spawn, post-teleport and others)
mechanics.note: Typed tickets with a level, a square radius and a lifetime (minecraft.wiki "Chunk"). The server adds the start ticket (level 32 - spawnChunkRadius, none at 0; it follows /gamerule) and, per player, a loading ticket over the view distance (level 31) and a simulation ticket (level 31 - simulation distance), as observed on both official servers; /forceload adds forced tickets (level 31), which persist
deviations: post-teleport, portal, ender pearl and dragon tickets have their types and levels but nothing creates them yet

mechanics.name: Ticket level propagation and entity-ticking versus block-ticking chunks
mechanics.note: Load and simulation levels: 31 and lower entity ticking, 32 block ticking, 33 border. Scheduled ticks, block events and block entities run at simulation level 32 and lower, entities at 31 and lower; a level without players or forced chunks stops its entities and block entities after 300 ticks. Ticket changes take effect in each level's chunk stage, after its scheduled ticks
deviations: new chunks load at once; the official servers take 2 to 4 ticks, varying between runs
entity ticking per ring is observed but not compared, because item physics differ (V07, C3)

mechanics.name: Unload and reload of chunks with pending ticks, block events and entities
mechanics.note: A dropped chunk's pending ticks keep their remaining delay, counted from the tick after it dropped; after a reload its scheduled ticks and block entities run again two ticks later and its block events at once (both official servers)
deviations: the official servers may keep a dropped chunk at border for one or two ticks and restore a cached chunk during the command or in the chunk stage, which moves restored ticks by a tick between runs; Circuit drops chunks at once and restores them in the chunk stage
entities of unloaded chunks are not reported as unloaded

mechanics.name: View distance and simulation distance
mechanics.note: Per player, a loading ticket of level 31 over the view distance (two rings beyond it loaded but not simulated) and a simulation ticket of level 31 - simulation distance; chunks loaded only by the view simulate nothing, as both official servers showed (ticking.js)
deviations: the view is not compared tick by tick with the official servers, whose chunk loading timing varies

mechanics.name: Sky light propagation
mechanics.note: Sky light from above the world, undiminished straight down through cells that dampen nothing, otherwise spreading like block light; computed from the blocks at the end of the previous tick

mechanics.name: Block light emission and propagation
mechanics.note: Emission, dampening and occlusion shape of every state of both versions match the official servers; light spreads one level per block, more through dampening blocks, never through faces that occlusion shapes close together
deviations: light at the edge of the loaded area is not compared

mechanics.name: Heightmaps
mechanics.note: The heightmaps clients get are computed from the blocks: WORLD_SURFACE, MOTION_BLOCKING (states that are solid or hold a fluid, minecraft.wiki "Heightmap") and, for 1.21.8, MOTION_BLOCKING_NO_LEAVES; which states count matches both official servers for every state
deviations: server-side heightmaps (OCEAN_FLOOR and the world-generation ones) are not kept; generation and mob spawning need them (C7, C8)

mechanics.name: Day-night cycle and time advancement
mechanics.note: The world's day time advances after each tick's commands while doDaylightCycle is on, persists and goes through Anvil import and export; /time sets and queries it with the official parser and replies; set_time goes to players on joining, every 20 ticks and on changes, as on both official servers
deviations: sleeping and the other behavior that depends on the time of day, except daylight detectors, is not modeled

mechanics.name: Rain, thunder, snow and their effects
mechanics.note: Rain and thunder flags with their timers and the clear timer, advanced while doWeatherCycle is on; rain and thunder levels fading by 0.01 a tick in single precision; /weather with the official parser and replies; the client events as both official servers send them, on joining too; saved in checkpoints and carried through Anvil (minecraft.wiki "Weather", "Commands/weather")
deviations: durations are drawn from Circuit's own stream, not the level's random sequence: the same ranges, other values
snow and ice, filling cauldrons, extinguishing fire, wet farmland and other effects of rain are not modeled; sleeping does not end the weather

mechanics.name: Lightning strikes and lightning rods
mechanics.note: Lightning is an entity: it follows the entity types of C3, then thunderstorms strike

mechanics.name: Block-event FIFO
mechanics.note: One FIFO per level with set semantics: events queued by commands, scheduled ticks and block entities run in queue order (those of the entity and block-entity phases in the next tick), an equal event is queued once, an event runs only if its block is still there, and events queued while events run join the queue; events of chunks that do not tick blocks wait, keeping their place, until they do

mechanics.name: Neighbor and shape update order and the chain limit
Entity tick order
deviations: ascending id, compared with the target versions for item entities only

mechanics.name: The level random source and its draw order
deviations: weather durations use Circuit's own derived stream, and other draws of the target versions (random ticks of blocks other than farmland, mobs and the rest) are not made yet
mechanics.note: Each level's java.util.Random-compatible sequence, its state saved with the world; fixtures seed it with 0 as the harness does and compare raw draw counts per stage

mechanics.name: Random-tick chunk order and positions
mechanics.note: Random ticks run at simulation level 31 and lower in 1.21.8, and at 32 and lower within 128 blocks of a non-spectator player in 1.21.4; on 1.21.8 every pick, the precipitation checks' draws and the chunk order of forced areas equal the official server's, with the level's position generator, the states that take random ticks as both versions report, and sections holding only water ticked too
deviations: the order of chunks that start ticking at different times is Circuit's model
1.21.4's order is not compared (the harness has no player to make its random ticks run)

mechanics.name: Biome allocation
mechanics.note: Every column is plains

mechanics.name: World presets (default, flat, large biomes, amplified, single biome, debug)
mechanics.note: A one-layer stone floor only

mechanics.name: Placed features: ores, trees, vegetation, lakes, geodes and others
Nether portal creation, search, scaling and arrival
End portals, strongholds and End gateways
Beds, respawn anchors and spawn points
deviations: respawn at the exact world spawn; the target version picks a random position around it

mechanics.name: Placement orientation and shapes: stairs, slabs, walls, fences, panes, doors, beds
deviations: only full cubes without properties, soul sand and mud, pillars, stairs, slabs, fences, panes, bars, walls, blocks facing the player, the clicked face or back along the view, rods, torches, lanterns, ladders, carpets, flowers, saplings, tall flowers, signs, banners, heads, beds and the blocks with block entities that use these rules (furnaces, smokers, blast furnaces, lecterns, beehives, ender chests, chiseled bookshelves, shulker boxes, barrels, beacons, jukeboxes, brewing stands, enchanting tables) are placed from their items besides the blocks with rules of their own; hanging signs and other blocks are not
spawners, sponges and test instance blocks are not placed
mechanics.note: Pillars along the clicked face's axis, stairs facing the player and in the clicked half, slabs in the clicked half and doubled, facing blocks toward the player or out of the clicked face, connectors and stairs with their neighbors' shapes, waterlogged in water sources, as both official servers do; every placed state checked against a report of every block item

mechanics.name: Fences, panes, bars and walls joining their neighbors
deviations: currents that push entities do not see waterlogged ones' water
mechanics.note: On shape updates and when a piston sets them down, as both official servers do; every state beside and above them compared

mechanics.name: Stairs taking corner shapes from the stairs beside them
deviations: currents that push entities do not see waterlogged ones' water
mechanics.note: On shape updates from the sides and when a piston sets them down, as both official servers do; every combination of stairs around them compared

mechanics.name: Torches, lanterns, ladders, carpets, flowers, saplings, signs and banners on their supports
deviations: flowers and saplings do not grow or spread (no random ticks for them)
other attached blocks (vines on walls, glow lichen, amethyst) are not modeled
a torch whose clicked side and floor both fail is not placed (the official servers also try the player's other looking directions)
mechanics.note: Placed by players where supported, and broken with their drops when the support goes (torches, lanterns, ladders, signs and banners on updates from their support's side, carpets, flowers and saplings on any update), as both official servers do; signs and banners stand and hang on solid blocks

mechanics.name: Two-part blocks: doors, beds, tall plants
deviations: tall grass, large ferns and other tall plants are not modeled
mechanics.note: Doors: the halves follow each other, a half without the other breaks (the lower one with the drop), and placed doors take their hinges as both official servers do; sunflowers, lilacs, rose bushes and peonies: placed with both halves, the lower one on soil, and both gone when either half or the soil goes (the lower one with the drop); beds: placed with both halves, the foot facing the player's way, a half leaving with the other, only the head dropping the bed

mechanics.name: Signs, banners, heads, pots and other block-entity data
mechanics.note: Block entities of blocks without rules of their own keep their saved data through checkpoints and Anvil interchange; one a player places starts empty and is written out as the official defaults of its type (every block's checked); nothing interprets the data, and clients do not receive it

mechanics.name: Copper weathering, waxing and scraping
mechanics.note: Copper blocks, cut copper, its stairs and slabs, chiseled copper, grates, bulbs, doors and trapdoors weather in random ticks by their chance and the copper around them, as the official 1.21.8 server does draw for draw
deviations: waxing with honeycomb and scraping with axes are not modeled
1.21.4's weathering is not compared (its random ticks run only near players, and the harness has none)

mechanics.name: Water flow, sources and washing away
Lava flow and lava-water interactions
mechanics.note: The overworld's lava; the Nether's, fire from lava and entities in lava are not modeled

mechanics.name: Waterlogged blocks
mechanics.note: Blocks waterlogged by placement in water, buckets and dispensers; their water moves to the sides their collision shapes leave open after shape updates and once poured; entities' currents do not see it yet

mechanics.name: Filling and emptying buckets
mechanics.note: Water and lava buckets filled and poured by players along their view and by dispensers; fish, axolotl and tadpole buckets, milk and placing powder snow are not modeled

mechanics.name: Fire spread, burning and extinguishing
mechanics.note: Fire stays on sturdy tops and beside flammable blocks, soul fire on soul sand and soil; its block ticks age it, burn it out, burn its neighbors by their burn odds and spread it by their ignite odds and the difficulty, as both official servers do; on 1.21.8 only near players unless allowFireTicksAwayFromPlayer; items and arrows in fire, soul fire and lava burn, by each version's timing in lava; lava sets fire beside the blocks it ignites in its random ticks, as the official 1.21.8 server does draw for draw; flint and steel and fire charges set fire beside the face used (where it can stay) and light campfires and candles, and flint and steel in dispensers sets fire in front, as both official servers do; players in fire catch fire from their 20th tick in it, burn (a hurt every 20 fire ticks, the on-fire flag), are set burning by lava for 15 seconds and put out by water and rain (1.21.8 with the extinguish sound for all, 1.21.4 for the others), as both official servers do
deviations: rain and humid biomes do not put fire blocks out sooner
entities other than items, arrows and players are not hurt or set burning
a player's fire ticks grow by one or two a tick in fire after catching it, by Circuit's own draws (the official servers' draws were not recorded tick by tick)
rain reaches a player with nothing above their feet or head that stops movement or holds a fluid (Circuit's rule; a player under a roof was not recorded)
lightning does not set fire
nether portals are not lit (C7)

mechanics.name: Snow, ice, freezing and melting
mechanics.note: Snow layers on their supports and breaking without them, snowy grass, podzol and mycelium, ice and frosted ice turning to water when players break them, frosted ice aging and melting in its block ticks and by updates, snow's drops, and players stacking snow layers and replacing single ones, as both official servers do; ice and snow layers melting by block light in random ticks, as the official 1.21.8 server does
deviations: freezing and melting by weather are not modeled
powder snow is not modeled

mechanics.name: Falling blocks: sand, gravel, concrete powder, anvils, dripstone, scaffolding
mechanics.note: Sand, red sand, gravel, the concrete powders and anvils: when they fall, the falling block's motion, landing, breaking into items, concrete powder in water, anvils wearing as they land by their own random (and gone when worn past damaged), and the 100- and 600-tick limits; pointed dripstone's thickness, its stalagmites breaking and stalactites falling and breaking where they land, and its growth and drips into cauldrons in random ticks
deviations: concrete powder placed beside water or reached by flowing water does not become concrete
scaffolding and suspicious sand and gravel do not fall
1.21.4's dripstone growth and drips are not compared (its random ticks run only near players, and the harness has none)
falling blocks hurt nothing

mechanics.name: Crop growth
mechanics.note: Wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroots and torchflower crops grow in random ticks with light 9 or more at their cell, by the farmland under and around them and the same crops beside them, beetroots and torchflowers skipping one tick in three, as the official 1.21.8 server does draw for draw; planted on farmland, and broken with their drops by an update that finds no farmland below
deviations: crops do not break in darkness
1.21.4's growth is not compared (its random ticks run only near players, and the harness has none)

mechanics.name: Farmland, hydration and trampling
mechanics.note: Farmland turns to dirt a tick after a solid block is set on it; entities count their falls and every landing on farmland draws its trampling check from the level random; in its random ticks it dries, is wetted by water and turns to dirt unless a crop or stem keeps it, as both official servers do
deviations: rain does not wet it
nothing tramples it (there are no living entities yet), and entities are not pushed up when it turns

mechanics.name: Other crops and plants: carrots, potatoes, beetroots, stems, sugar cane, cactus, bamboo, kelp, cocoa, berries, nether wart, chorus
mechanics.note: Carrots, potatoes, beetroots, stems, torchflower crops, nether wart, sweet berry bushes and bamboo grow on their ground only and break when it goes; sugar cane needs water beside its ground and cacti nothing solid beside them, both breaking a tick after an update finds them unsupported; melon and pumpkin stems grow and set their fruit on farmland or dirt, and attached stems stand ripe again when it goes; sugar cane, cacti and their flowers, nether wart, sweet berry bushes, cocoa, kelp, weeping, twisting and cave vines and bamboo grow and mushrooms spread in random ticks, as the official 1.21.8 server does draw for draw
deviations: chorus flowers and saplings do not grow
1.21.4's growth is not compared (its random ticks run only near players, and the harness has none)
cacti hurt only items
chorus and pitcher crops are not supported yet
without data packs, plants whose loot rolls random numbers drop nothing

mechanics.name: Saplings, trees and leaf decay
mechanics.note: Leaves take their distance from logs through block ticks after updates, as both official servers do, and decay at distance 7 unless persistent in random ticks with their loot, as the official 1.21.8 server does
deviations: saplings do not grow into trees
scaffolding's distance is not seen by leaves
1.21.4's decay is not compared (its random ticks run only near players, and the harness has none)

mechanics.name: Grass, mycelium, nylium, moss and sculk spread
mechanics.note: Grass blocks and mycelium die under blocks their light cannot pass and under water, and spread to dirt within reach in random ticks, and nylium under such blocks becomes netherrack, as the official 1.21.8 server does draw for draw
deviations: nylium, moss and sculk do not spread
1.21.4's spreading is not compared (its random ticks run only near players, and the harness has none)

mechanics.name: Bone meal
mechanics.note: Dispensers' bone meal on crops, stems, cocoa, berry bushes, bamboo, dripleaves, petals and vines, used up only when it acts, as both official servers do draw for draw; players' bone meal acts the same way
deviations: players' bone meal is not compared
saplings, grass, moss, mushrooms and nylium (their features), glow lichen, sea pickles, seagrass, coral and propagules take none

mechanics.name: Coral dying without water
deviations: coral blocks and plants (not fans) are inert
currents that push entities do not see waterlogged fans' water
mechanics.note: Coral fans and wall fans of every kind die 60 to 99 ticks (a level-random draw) after they are left without water, when placed or updated; they need a sturdy top or face and leave their water when they break; pistons break living fans and move dead ones

mechanics.name: Redstone dust power, shapes and steps
Strong and weak power through solid blocks
mechanics.note: Every state of both versions conducts or not as both official servers report; the rules' answer for blocks with rules of their own matches as well

mechanics.name: Support of components
mechanics.note: Every state's support shape from the registry (collision/support): floor torches and pressure plates on a top whose middle bears them, dust, levers, buttons and wall torches on whole faces

mechanics.name: Redstone torches and burnout
deviations: players place torches on the clicked face, not by their view
floor support comes from collision shapes
no burnout sound or smoke
mechanics.note: Floor and wall torches power every neighbor but their block and the block above them strongly; power in their block turns them off two ticks after an update; the eighth turn-off of a position within 60 ticks burns a torch out for 160 ticks

mechanics.name: Buttons, pressure plates, tripwire and targets
deviations: tripwire is not modeled
no mobs or players press plates yet; only arrows press wooden buttons
of the projectiles only arrows and snowballs hit target blocks
mechanics.note: Buttons of every kind on floors, walls and ceilings: 20 ticks for stone and polished blackstone, 30 for wooden ones, which arrows press and hold; pressure plates of every kind sensing the entities on them (weighted ones counting them); target blocks grading projectile hits

mechanics.name: Daylight detectors, sculk sensors, lightning rods and other sources
deviations: sculk sensors, lightning rods and the other sensors are not modeled
mechanics.note: Daylight detectors, normal and inverted, set their output every 20 game ticks from the sky light in their cell, the time of day, rain and thunder; using one inverts it at once

mechanics.name: Doors, trapdoors, fence gates, note blocks, bells, copper bulbs and other consumers
deviations: bells, copper bulbs and the other consumers are not modeled
player heads with a note block sound of their own play nothing
mechanics.note: Doors, trapdoors and fence gates of every kind open and close with the power around them and by hand (iron ones only by power), quietly, with a level-random draw for the sound; note blocks take the instrument of the block below or a head above and play on a rising signal and when used, as block events that draw for the sound

mechanics.name: Rails, powered, detector and activator rails
deviations: waterlogging is stored only
activator rails act on no minecart (only empty ones exist, which they leave unchanged)
comparators read 0 from detector rails (no minecart has contents)
mechanics.note: Rails take their shapes from the rails beside them and make them join, curve with the official preferences, rise toward higher rails, switch at three-way junctions on updates from signal sources and need a sturdy top; powered and activator rails pass power along up to eight rails of their kind; detector rails sense minecarts, check every 20 ticks and power their ends, neighbors and the block below

mechanics.name: Comparator readings of every container and special block
mechanics.note: Chests and hoppers

mechanics.name: Lecterns
mechanics.note: A writable or written book goes on a lectern without one (the item tag lectern_books; used up outside creative mode); its window turns to the previous or next page, to a page by its number or takes the book, a click on its slot takes the book too and the window closes without it; a page turn powers the lectern until its block tick 2 ticks later, every neighbor and the block below strongly, a turn while powered adding nothing; comparators read 1 more than 14 times the page's place, dust connects to it, and a removed lectern's book pops out on top toward its front; the harness traces and a 22-step client scenario match both official servers
deviations: a book put on from the off hand is not modeled
written books' pages are not resolved for the player who puts them on

mechanics.name: Honey blocks and slime-honey separation
deviations: entities other than items and primed TNT do not slide down honey
mechanics.note: Sticky in piston structures but not to slime; slows what moves on it to 40%; items and primed TNT slide down its sides; moving sideways it carries what stands on it

mechanics.name: Blocks destroyed by pistons and their drops
Moving blocks pushing entities and players
deviations: stuck-entity and piston-base corrections are not modeled
mechanics.note: Entities pushed out of the space a moving block sweeps through each step (0.01 beyond it, at most 0.51 a tick on each axis); moving blocks collide where they stand; moving slime blocks set the speed along their motion to one block a tick; slime blocks bounce what lands on them at 80%

mechanics.name: Push reactions of every block (immovable, destroy, block entities)
mechanics.note: Every block of both versions is moved (pushed and pulled), destroyed, pushed only or left in place as the official servers' pistons treat it; moved blocks arrive without their water

mechanics.name: Dispensers and droppers with dispense behaviors
deviations: dispensed projectiles, fire, shears, boats, bottles, honeycomb, glowstone and water bottles at their targets, golem and wither heads, other fluids, other minecarts, spawn eggs, armor stands and shulker boxes are not modeled: those items stay

armor goes onto the first player by key but spectators whose standing box meets the cell in front (a crouching player's lower box is not used), and also onto a dead player who has not respawned (none of it recorded); heads and saddles still eject
level events are sent for items a dispenser ejects (not minecarts off rails) and armor put on only, not for droppers, the other uses or a dispenser that fails
mechanics.note: Fired 4 ticks after power reaches them or the block above them, from a random filled slot (level-random draws); droppers fill the container in front or eject; dispensers eject items (position, motion and draws exact), prime TNT, pour and fill water and lava buckets, set minecarts on rails, put armor and elytras on the player in front whose slot for it is empty (else eject them), with their sound and smoke (level events 1000 and 2000)

mechanics.name: The Crafter
mechanics.note: Crafters triggered by power at the block craft their grid 4 ticks later by the official data packs' crafting recipes, deliver the result and the remainders to the container in front or throw them out whole as dispensers throw items, show that they crafted for 6 ticks, fill evenly from hoppers and droppers, give items to hoppers and drive comparators by their filled slots, as both official servers do tick by tick

mechanics.name: Trapped chests and chest openers
mechanics.note: Trapped chests pair with trapped chests only and are containers as chests are; each chest half counts the players viewing it and queues its lid's block event with the count at every change and every 5-tick recheck while viewed; a trapped chest gives its count as power on every side and strongly to the block below, and dust connects to it; the harness traces and a 14-step client scenario with two players match both official servers
deviations: the open and close sounds and the game events sculk sensors hear are not modeled

mechanics.name: Barrels
mechanics.note: Barrels facing any side are 27-slot containers that hoppers fill and empty and comparators read, conducting power as solid blocks; they open under a solid block, are open from their first viewer to their last by the viewer counts and rechecks of chests (no block events), keep an open state they were set to, and drop their contents when removed; the harness traces and client scenarios match both official servers
deviations: the open and close sounds and the game events sculk sensors hear are not modeled

mechanics.name: Composters
mechanics.note: Items compost by the wiki's chances, drawn from the level random (the first item into an empty composter always adds a layer), below level 7, from players and through the top from hoppers, droppers and crafters one item at a time; full composters get ready 20 ticks later; players and hoppers below take the bone meal; a broken ready composter drops it; comparators read the level; the harness traces (every compostable item of both versions) and a client scenario match both official servers
deviations: villagers composting and the sounds are not modeled

mechanics.name: Ender chests
mechanics.note: Each player's 27-slot ender inventory, saved with the player and kept on death, through every ender chest's window; viewers counted with lid events and rechecks as chests; no opening under a conductor; comparators, hoppers and pistons do not act on them; drops by the loot table; the harness trace and a two-player client scenario match both official servers
deviations: the open and close sounds and the game events sculk sensors hear are not modeled
ender inventories are not carried through Anvil import and export (player data is not)

mechanics.name: Shulker boxes
mechanics.note: 27-slot containers of every color facing any side that refuse shulker boxes, open only when their lid can rise, count their viewers with lid events (no rechecks), and drop one item keeping their contents and name, which gives them back when placed; a creative player's break drops a filled box only; the harness trace and client scenarios match both official servers
deviations: the lid's push of entities, the neighbor updates when it finishes opening or closing, and the sounds are not modeled
without data packs a broken box drops its contents beside it
Anvil interchange refuses items whose container component holds stacks

mechanics.name: Chiseled bookshelves
mechanics.note: Six book slots shown in the block state, filled and emptied by players by the sixth of the front they click, filled by hoppers and droppers and emptied by hoppers below; comparators read the last slot touched; the harness trace and a client scenario match both official servers
deviations: the sounds are not modeled

mechanics.name: Component-aware automation (stacking of items with components)
mechanics.note: Stacks merge only with equal item, damage and components; hoppers, pickups, inserts and menus keep components

mechanics.name: TNT placement and breaking
mechanics.note: TNT placed by commands, pistons and players becomes primed TNT where redstone reaches it; broken, it drops itself by its loot table
deviations: unstable TNT is not primed when broken

mechanics.name: Ignition by redstone, fire, flint and steel, fire charges, burning projectiles and explosions
mechanics.note: Redstone: a signal from any neighbor when TNT is placed, moved in by a piston or updated (blocks, levers, diodes, observers, dust, strongly powered blocks); explosions prime TNT with a fuse of 10 to 29 ticks; fire burning it primes it; a burning arrow primes the TNT it hits; dispensers prime TNT items; flint and steel and fire charges a player uses on TNT prime it, and so does flint and steel in a dispenser
deviations: fire charges from dispensers (small fireballs) are not modeled; of the burning projectiles only arrows are modeled

mechanics.name: Primed TNT entities: fuse, motion, collision and removal
mechanics.note: Creation before the block goes, launch from the level random, the fuse, gravity, collision, ground friction, currents after the move, chunk edges, falling below the world without being removed; it explodes when the fuse runs out and is pushed by other explosions
deviations: lava, bubble columns, portals and entity pushing do not move primed TNT

mechanics.name: Explosions: affected blocks, resistance, fluids, drops, chain reactions, damage and knockback
mechanics.note: TNT's explosion: rays with single-precision intensity and blast resistance (waterlogged blocks resist as water), the reached cells in hash-set order shuffled by the level random, entities hurt and pushed first by distance and exposure (items destroyed or left with less health; nether stars immune; primed TNT pushed from its feet), then blocks cleared with drops merged into stacks of 16, TNT primed with a 10-29 tick fuse, nothing out of the world's height
deviations: entities of one chunk section are hurt in id order, not the order they entered the section
explosions do not hurt or push players yet
a hash-set bucket of eight or more cells (Java turns it into a tree) is ordered as a list

mechanics.name: Live fuses across save, reload and unload
mechanics.note: Fuse, position and motion kept by checkpoints, Anvil and unloading chunks
deviations: after an unload the official servers run a pending tick of the chunk one tick later than Circuit in trace/tnt_reload_pending (their unload timing varies; Circuit unloads dropped chunks at once)

mechanics.name: The tntExplodes game rule
mechanics.note: With the rule off, 1.21.8 does not prime TNT at all; the 1.21.4 harness refuses the skeleton, and 1.21.4 always primes TNT

mechanics.name: Creeper, bed, respawn anchor, end crystal, wither and wind charge explosions
TNT duplication with a named design
deviations: only the Mytteri push duper is established; other designs are untested
reloading its chunk follows the chunk unload timing deviation (open trace tnt_duper_reload)
mechanics.note: The Mytteri push duper primes its TNT on every push after the first while the block moves on, as both official servers do, over eight pushes, in each horizontal direction and across chunk edges and corners, with its documented cobblestone wall (tnt_duper_wall; the earlier traces use stone); restored engines continue it exactly

mechanics.name: Flying machines
deviations: only two-way engine A and the vertical two-way slim engine are established; docks and larger machines are untested
mechanics.note: Two documented engines fly in all six directions with cargo, across chunk edges and into obstacles, as both official servers do

mechanics.name: Gravity-block machines and duplication
deviations: gravity-block duplication needs end portals and is not supported
mechanics.note: Sand and gravel in piston machines (carried by slime, pushed off ledges, dropped by pulled supports, landing on moving pistons) as both official servers do

mechanics.name: Bedrock breaking
mechanics.note: The method documented in text for 1.21 (minecraft.wiki "Tutorial:Breaking bedrock", exploding piston) has a player place a piston while TNT explodes beside them, which needs player-timed placement and explosions that hurt players (C6); the headless-piston method is documented only in videos

mechanics.name: Item sorters, clocks and pulse circuits
mechanics.note: The documented basic hopper item sorter as a whole machine (sorting across a chunk edge, overflow protection); documented pulse generators and limiters; clocks as component cases
deviations: other sorter designs, clocks, pulse extenders and edge detectors are not established as machines

mechanics.name: Typed entities with UUIDs, attributes and components
deviations: the engine models item entities only (more kinds follow in C3.3 and C3.4)
entity UUIDs are derived from ids by the server, not world state (C11)
mechanics.note: Explicit kind, double-precision state, tick count, signed age

mechanics.name: Entity tracking ranges, metadata and visibility for clients
mechanics.note: Items and players

mechanics.name: Entity persistence across save and reload
mechanics.note: Item entities saved with their chunk come back a tick after it reloads, under new ids with new tick counts; checkpoints keep entities waiting to come back
deviations: recovery after a restart keeps ids and tick counts, where an official server loads entities with new ones

mechanics.name: Entity sections, migration between chunks and unloaded chunks
deviations: entities of a reloaded chunk come back in coordinate order, not the official chunk-map order
mechanics.note: Items stop ticking in chunks that are not entity ticking and collide with unloaded cells as with full blocks

mechanics.name: Item entity motion and collision
deviations: moving blocks push items differently (trace/item_piston_push)
entities of a reloaded chunk come back in coordinate order, not the official chunk-map order
mechanics.note: Double-precision gravity, drag, collision with every state's collision boxes, bouncing, the resting rule, currents and buoyancy in water (water surfaces in single precision), damage from cacti, burning in fire, soul fire and lava and floating in lava (netherite), moving out of blocks (through the nearest face free of a full cube, at a speed from the item's own random, through blocks), identical with both official servers in the passing traces

mechanics.name: Item merging
mechanics.note: Every 40 ticks of the item's own count, or every 2 after a move into another block; reach half a block sideways; stacks of one kind within their limit; the smaller joins the larger (equal: the other survives); younger age and longer pickup delay kept

mechanics.name: Pickup by players and hoppers, pickup delays
Despawning
mechanics.note: Age 6000, -32768 never; the age goes up after the item's move and merges

mechanics.name: Experience orbs
mechanics.note: Experience orbs fall, slide, bounce on the ground (each version its own way), float with their eye in water, jump in lava, take in orbs of their value 40 ids apart every 20 ticks, move out of blocks (each version its own way) and go at age 6000, as both official servers do tick by tick; experience comes in orbs of the official values that join orbs nearby by a draw of 40; mined ores and sculk give theirs, Silk Touch none; players within 8 blocks draw orbs and take one every 2 ticks, gaining the official servers' levels, totals and progress
deviations: how players draw orbs is not compared tick by tick
Mending and death drops of experience are not modeled
mobs, breeding, fishing and trading give no experience yet

mechanics.name: Arrows, tridents, thrown items, potions, fireworks, wind charges and fishing bobbers
mechanics.note: Arrows and snowballs (summoned): flight, drag in air and water, sticking 0.05 short of the shape they hit, falling again when their block goes, life and despawn, fire counted down and put out by water, burning arrows priming TNT, snowballs breaking on blocks
deviations: projectiles pass through entities
bows, crossbows, dispensers and players do not shoot
currents do not push arrows
tridents, thrown potions, eggs, ender pearls, fireworks, wind charges and fishing bobbers are missing
after an unload the official servers remove a chunk's arrows a tick later than Circuit in trace/arrow_reload (their unload timing varies)

mechanics.name: Boats and rafts
mechanics.note: Empty boats and rafts (summoned): floating with buoyancy, sinking under water, sliding on land with the slipperiness under them, falling, landing on the surface from the air, currents, pushing each other
deviations: a boat floating on still water differs from the official vertical velocity in the last bits after a few ticks (trace/boat_motion; positions stay within 2.2e-16)
riders and paddling
chest boats
bubble columns

mechanics.name: Minecarts of every kind
mechanics.note: Empty minecarts (summoned) off rails — falling, the 0.4 (0.2 in water) speed limit, halving on the ground, 5% drag in the air, water as their last tick ended — and on rails: following the rail's line at up to 0.4 a tick, 4% drag, speeding up down slopes and slowing up them, turning through curves, stopped by blocks, braked by unpowered and boosted by powered powered rails; minecarts collide with each other's and boats' boxes and push each other by their yaw
deviations: a moving minecart picks up the boats it touches (riding is not modeled; it neither picks them up nor pushes them)
yaw from an exact arctangent (the official servers use an approximation; only the push test reads it)
chest, hopper, furnace, TNT, spawner and command block minecarts
riders

mechanics.name: Happy Ghast harnesses and leash changes
Survival, creative and spectator modes
mechanics.note: /gamemode's abilities, game mode event and the player list's game mode as both official servers send them; spectators seen by spectators only, invisible, flying through blocks, opening windows without using or taking anything, taking an entity's view by attacking it until the shift key, teleporting by the spectator menu; the shift key's flag and the crouching pose shown to others
deviations: adventure and hardcore modes are not modeled
a spectator's windows other than a chest's (an ender chest's and a lectern's not opened) were not recorded

mechanics.name: Movement checks against block shapes, step-up and corrections
mechanics.note: Walking, jumping and sprinting

mechanics.name: Swimming, crawling, climbing, elytra flight and sleeping
Interaction reach and dig timing
mechanics.note: Reach for blocks and containers; dig time from documented values, with haste, conduit power and mining fatigue (the documented factors, as both official servers count haste 0 and 1, conduit power 1 and mining fatigue 0)

mechanics.name: Health, hunger, saturation, exhaustion and regeneration
mechanics.note: Food from eating and drinking (eating_and_drinking); regeneration up to the maximum health while the naturalRegeneration game rule allows; on joining, health and then experience follow the inventory, the position and the first tick's recipe unlocks as on both official servers

mechanics.name: Damage sources and the hurt cooldown
mechanics.note: Falls (beyond the safe fall distance: on 1.21.8 with the move that lands, rounded down; on 1.21.4 without it, rounded up), the void, starvation, the effects' magic and wither damage, fire (in_fire), burning (on_fire), lava and magma blocks (hot_floor); fire resistance keeps fire's damage off; armor wears and reduces the damage it reduces (not the bypasses_armor tag's), resistance takes 20% a level, absorption takes damage first; damage that tires costs its exhaustion; the damage event, the hurt sound by the damage type's effects (hurt_on_fire for the burning types), death and fall sounds for the others nearby and the velocity at the next entity update, as both official servers send them
deviations: the velocity told is that of a player standing still, or at the bottom of lava (players hurt in the air, moving or in water were not recorded)
the fall sound of the block landed on is not played
the hurt and death sounds' pitches come from Circuit's own draws
drowning, suffocation, cactus, sweet berry bushes, freezing, campfires and the fireDamage game rule are not modeled

a magma block hurts a player standing on its edge by the nearest block under them that bears them (minecraft.wiki; not recorded); lava halves the distance fallen each tick by minecraft.wiki (not recorded)

mechanics.name: Death, drops and respawning
deviations: death drops spread in a fixed pattern
where a player appears around the spawn is drawn from Circuit's own random (the official servers draw it from theirs), in at most 16 columns
mechanics.note: The death screen and the death message with the player's name as both official servers write it, the death animation (entity event 3), the body kept in the others' view (its health 0 and velocity told) until it goes after the death animation (entity event 60; Circuit takes 20 ticks) or the player respawns; the respawn's packets Circuit sends in the official order, with the operator level; new and respawning players placed in a random column within the spawnRadius game rule

mechanics.name: Melee attacks, attack cooldown, critical hits, sweeping and knockback
Armor protection, toughness and shields
mechanics.note: Armor's points, toughness and netherite's knockback resistance as attribute modifiers of each armor slot, as both official servers send them; damage armor reduces (not in the bypasses_armor damage type tag: fire, lava and magma blocks so far) is reduced by the documented formula, to the float as both official servers reduce it, and wears each piece worn by a quarter of it, at least one (netherite not by fire), through the rules at the next tick, breaking it at its durability
deviations: a piece's breaking has no sound or entity event (not modeled, as for tools; not recorded), and the unbreakable component is not honored
protection enchantments, unbreaking and shields are not modeled

mechanics.name: Status effects
deviations: slow falling changes nothing (fall damage is taken in full), nor do water breathing, the omens (but for the sound each makes when it comes) and the effects that act on death or when hurt; of the attributes effects change, the movement and attack speed and luck only reach the client
amplifiers above 28 of instant health and damage double without the official servers' integer overflow (not recorded)
only players have effects; /effect takes players by name, @s, @p, @a and @e
of the shared flags sprinting's is not sent yet
on 1.21.4 the health regenerated after a levitation's fall differs from the fourth heal (0.33 points where the official server healed 0.5); the fall itself hurts as on both official servers
a player's effects come in id order and players' entity data of one tick in the order they connected; the official servers' orders are their own (for effects one that varies from run to run)
the entity data of a command's effects comes in the next tick, 50 ms after the effect packet, where the official 1.21.8 server took 80 ms (25 ms or more on both official servers)
mechanics.note: /effect give and clear with the official parser and replies; an effect given again combines with the one a player has (a stronger level replacing it with the old one underneath while it lasts longer, the same amplifier lengthening it, a weaker longer level underneath), every level counts down (one underneath that runs out is shown with no time left when the level above it ends, and the effect is removed in that tick, with any level still under it), an effect is sent again at each multiple of 600 ticks left and removed when it ends; the effect packets go to the player at once and the entity data they decide (invisibility and glowing flags, effect particles, ambience) in the next tick to the player and to whoever sees them; levitating players are not kicked for flying; effects are saved with the player and sent on joining; a respawned player has none; the effects that heal, hurt or feed act by the time their shown level has left before each tick and their amplifier: instant health and damage, hunger and saturation every tick they last, regeneration, poison and wither every 50, 25 and 40 ticks halved per level, through the hurt cooldown; absorption ends once its absorption is used up, and an omen that comes plays its sound to everyone nearby; foods, potions and ominous bottles give effects (eating_and_drinking); resistance takes 20% of damage a level and fire resistance keeps off fire's, as both official servers reduce it

mechanics.name: Attributes and modifiers
deviations: only players have attributes, and only those Circuit models: the armor and its toughness, the movement and attack speed, the attack damage, both reaches, knockback resistance, luck, the maximum health and absorption and the safe fall distance
the movement and attack speed, the reaches and luck only reach the client: Circuit's movement checks do not use the speed, and it has no attacks or rolls with luck
a packet's attributes come in id order; the official servers' order varies from run to run
players' health and skin entity data (indexes 9 and 17), which the official servers send around the attributes on joining, to those who see a player and when the health changes, are not sent
mechanics.note: A player's attributes as both official servers keep and send them: the armor slots' armor, toughness and knockback resistance and the main hand weapon's or tool's attack damage and speed (client/armor; added again, last, whenever the slot's stack changes, its wear included); the movement speed and both reaches from the first join, those effects change from then on, kept across respawns and saved; creative mode's reach, sprinting and the effects' modifiers (speed, slowness, haste, mining fatigue, jump boost, health boost, absorption, luck, bad luck; strength and weakness on the attack damage by minecraft.wiki, which the official servers do not send) by amplifier, added again at the end of the list whenever an effect's shown level is given, changed, lengthened or comes back; sent after the next tick's entity data to the player and to whoever sees them, with a player who appears, before the health on a rejoin or respawn (those who see them get them twice) and after it on a first join; the maximum health (regeneration, rejoins, the health cut when it falls), absorption and the safe fall distance applied

mechanics.name: Placing blocks from items
mechanics.note: 17 item cases, building blocks on both versions (client/building), and every placed state of every block item in fifteen contexts (placement/official_items)

mechanics.name: Tools, durability and harvest rules
mechanics.note: Pickaxes and axes

mechanics.name: Eating and drinking
mechanics.note: Every food of both versions, milk, potions and ominous bottles: a use refused at full hunger in survival for all but the always eaten, lasting 32 ticks (dried kelp 16, honey 40), shown by the living flags and heard by others; when it runs out the item used up (not in creative mode) with its bowl, bucket or bottle left, then, in the order both official servers act: the finished use's event, a suspicious stew's effects, a food's sound and burp, a potion's and an ominous bottle's effects, milk and honey clearing effects, a chorus fruit's teleport with its event, sound and cooldown, the item's own effects by their chances, the food and saturation, the health packet, the living flags and the slot; the 18 kinds client/eat eats compared, the others from minecraft-data and minecraft.wiki
deviations: a stack's own food, consumable, use remainder and use cooldown components and 1.21.8's potion duration scale are not read: each item eats as its kind does by default

a chorus fruit's tries follow minecraft.wiki (up to 16 within 8 blocks, down to the ground, where the player fits out of fluids), drawn from Circuit's own random, with a position sent for each try that finds ground: both official servers sent one to nine positions in a use and failed more tries than Circuit does, by rules not determined
the chances of raw chicken's, rotten flesh's and poisonous potatoes' effects (minecraft.wiki), and the volume and pitch of the use sounds, are drawn from Circuit's own random

the foods eaten at full hunger beyond honey and chorus fruit (golden apples, suspicious stew), the chance effects, a remainder going into the inventory or thrown out, and spectating or death ending a use were not recorded
a use in progress and item cooldowns are not saved

mechanics.name: Other item uses: buckets, shears, flint and steel, bone meal, spawn eggs, fishing, maps, books
mechanics.note: Flint and steel and fire charges: fire beside the face used where it can stay, campfires, candles and candle cakes lit, TNT primed, the level random's sound draws, flint and steel worn by one (and gone at its durability) and fire charges used up outside creative mode, flint and steel in dispensers. Shears: pumpkins carved (facing the face used or the player, four seeds out of it), full beehives and bee nests emptied of three honeycomb (also by dispensers), cobwebs, leaves, wool, vines and glow lichen cut at their tool component's speeds, tripwire disarmed when broken, every block broken wearing them. Knowledge books: the recipes they name given when every one is a recipe (none otherwise), the book used up outside creative mode. As both official servers do
deviations: spawn eggs, fishing and books are not modeled here; buckets, bone meal and maps are covered by their own families
shears on sheep, mooshrooms, snow golems and bogged (C8), and the bees an emptied hive angers, are not modeled
the use sounds are not sent

mechanics.name: Equipment slots and wearing armor
mechanics.note: Armor slots accept armor; armor and elytras put on by use from either hand (swapping with what is worn, in creative mode too, where with nothing worn a copy goes on; not a carved pumpkin or a zombie head), by clicks and by dispensers, with their equip sounds (not when taken off; the creative inventory's and a pumpkin's or head's worn by clicks not recorded); what a player holds and wears shown to others when it changes (the hands swapped as entity event 55) and when the player appears; the attributes armor and held weapons give
deviations: curse of binding, the turtle shell's water breathing, the elytra's gliding, leather armor against freezing and golden armor with piglins are not modeled

mechanics.name: Player window, chest, double-chest and hopper menus with every click mode
Crafting (2x2 and table) and the recipe book
deviations: recipes whose results carry components (suspicious stew) make nothing
among several kinds of items for one ingredient, placing a recipe from the book takes them in the order the inventory first holds them; the official servers' choice varies from run to run
the recipes unlocked in one tick come in advancement id order (the official servers' order varies); advancement packets are not sent
placing a recipe from the book sends the grid's result once when it changed; the official servers send it again for each grid change the placement makes (the same window either way)
without the official data pack there are no recipes
mechanics.note: The player's 2x2 grid and the crafting table's 3x3 grid craft with the shaped, shapeless and transmute recipes of the loaded data packs: the result follows the grid, every click mode takes it, ingredients are used and remainders kept, and the grids go back to the inventory on closing and drop when the player leaves or dies; 48 steps in the own window and 47 at crafting tables give the same windows as both official servers. The recipe book shows every recipe's display, and the data packs' recipe advancements unlock recipes as both official servers do (items in the inventory, filled slots, the first tick, water, crafting, /recipe), with seen recipes and the books' settings kept; recipes placed from the book fill the own grid, crafting tables and furnaces, with ghosts for missing items, as both official servers place them, and a crafting table makes the placed recipe until its grid changes; with doLimitedCrafting on, the grids make only known recipes, a result already shown staying until the grid changes. Repairing, armor dye, banner copying, shield decoration, firework stars, rockets, star fades, book and map cloning, map extending, tipped arrows and decorated pots are made at crafting tables and in crafters as on both official servers (an extended map becoming a new map with the map ids each way of taking it uses), special recipes matching in id order with the others; recipes match and the book numbers them by the id's path, then its namespace, as both official servers order recipes of several namespaces; and each change a click makes to a grid's slot sends its result again as they do

mechanics.name: Furnaces, smokers, blast furnaces and campfires
mechanics.note: Furnaces, smokers and blast furnaces burn their fuel and cook by the official data packs' recipes (the first by the id's path, then its namespace), light and go out, fill and empty through hoppers by their faces and drive comparators, as both official servers do tick by tick; every item's burn time as both report it
deviations: an experience's rest below 1 comes by a random of Circuit's own, where the official servers draw from an unseeded random
several recipes give their experience in recipe id order, the official servers in a hash order
campfires do not cook

mechanics.name: Stonecutters
mechanics.note: Stonecutters cut by the data packs' stonecutting recipes: clients receive the recipes in the official order (by id path, then namespace) with the item property sets, a button chooses one of the input's recipes, every click mode takes the result, the input goes back on closing and drops when the player leaves; 27 steps and the recipe packet give the same windows and data as both official servers

mechanics.name: Smithing tables
mechanics.note: Smithing tables upgrade (the base's damage and components kept) and trim (the addition's material in the recipe's or template's pattern) by the data packs' smithing recipes; each slot takes what some recipe takes there, quick moves route by them, taking the result uses one of each input; 24 steps give the same windows and components as both official servers
deviations: on 1.21.5 and later, trim materials come from the vanilla materials' items, not from the items' provides_trim_material component

mechanics.name: Grindstones
mechanics.note: Grindstones take what wears or holds enchantments; one input loses all but its curses (an enchanted book becomes a book), two of a kind merge their durabilities with 5% of the most and the curses of both; the repair cost counts the curses kept; quick moves fill the upper input, then the lower; 25 steps give the same windows and components as both official servers
deviations: taking a result gives experience drawn from the level random, so the client scenario checks only its range
stacks with several enchantments keep them in ascending id order; the official servers keep a hash order of their own, which their windows show

mechanics.name: Looms
mechanics.note: Looms offer the patterns of the banner pattern tag no_item_required, or a pattern item's own, in the tags' order; a button chooses one while a banner and a dye are there, and the result is the banner with that pattern's layer in the dye's color on top (also beyond six layers); the choice follows the slots as on both official servers; taking the result uses a banner and a dye; 32 steps give the same windows and components as both official servers

mechanics.name: Brewing stands
mechanics.note: Brewing stands take blaze powder as fuel for 20 brews, brew for 400 ticks each bottle that mixes with the ingredient into its mix (every mix of both official servers' brewing reports), stop when the ingredient changes or nothing is left to brew, throw out dragon's breath's glass bottle, show their bottles, take from and give to hoppers by face and drive comparators, as both official servers do tick by tick (with the official data packs); players use their menus as on both official servers, and a brewed bottle is a new one of its mix without the old one's other components

mechanics.name: Anvils
mechanics.note: Anvils repair with their items' materials and by combining two of a kind, join enchantments from books and like items within their highest levels, supported items and exclusive sets, and rename by the typed name (filtered and at most 50 UTF-16 code units, kept for the next items, compared with the names items show in English); prior work penalties, the 39-level cap for renaming, too expensive results and the level cost taken from the player as both official servers give them; the /xp command sets and adds levels and points; 48 steps give the same windows, costs, components and experience as both official servers
deviations: an anvil wears by a random of Circuit's own; the official servers draw it from an unseeded random
stacks with several enchantments keep the left's order with the new ones after it; the official servers keep a hash order of their own
names items show come from the jar's English names: a written book's title, a player head's owner and item_name components are not used

mechanics.name: Enchanting tables
mechanics.note: Enchanting tables make three offers from the bookshelves around them (the power provider and transmitter block tags) and the player's enchantment seed: their level costs, the enchantments each shows and their levels, drawn as both official servers draw them from the data packs' in_enchanting_table enchantments, weights, cost ranges, primary items and exclusive sets and the wiki's enchantability by material; an offer is taken for its place in levels and lapis (any in creative mode), a book becoming an enchanted book that loses one enchantment; 320 windows of the official servers with two other seeds and a 97-step scenario and a 64-step survey give the same windows, offers, enchantments and levels as both official servers
deviations: a new player's enchantment seed and the seed after enchanting are Circuit's own; the official servers draw them at random
stacks with several enchantments keep the order they were drawn in; the official servers keep a hash order of their own

mechanics.name: Cartography tables
mechanics.note: The cartography table's window copies a filled map with an empty map, zooms it with paper to a new map of the next scale (up to 4) and locks it with a glass pane to a new locked map, taking only the items each slot takes, with shift-clicks, as both official servers do (with the official data packs)

mechanics.name: Beacons
mechanics.note: Beacons count their pyramids of the beacon_base_blocks tag and look up their beams every 80 game ticks, give the powers their window chose (paid with an item of the beacon_payment_items tag, which closing the window throws out) to the players but spectators in range (up by the world's height), and play their activate, ambient, deactivate (also when removed) and power_select sounds; a 35-step scenario with two players and a 15-step scenario of payments left in the window, spectators, players far above, a beacon without levels removed and a named beacon give the same windows, properties, effects, sounds, item entities and block entity data as both official servers
deviations: the beam is looked up whole at each cycle; how the official servers follow a beam changing far up between cycles was not recorded

mechanics.name: Loot tables for blocks, entities and containers

deviations: maps in the Nether do not explore (the official servers draw a pattern not described publicly); banners and item frames are not modeled
signs and displays are not shown; books given unresolved are not resolved when opened
mechanics.note: Empty maps become filled maps of new maps, and the players carrying them get their data and markers (on the map, on its edge, or none far off), as both official servers send them; maps held in a hand explore the terrain around their holder, every block state's color, shading and water depth drawn as both official servers draw them. A book and quill in a hotbar slot or the off hand takes the pages a client edits (100 of 1024 code units at most, kept as sent) and is signed into a written book (a title of 32 at most, the player as author, generation 0, pages as plain text, resolved), and a written book opens for reading and is copied with books and quills, and filled maps with empty maps, and filled maps are extended with paper into new maps of the next scale at crafting tables and in crafters, as both official servers do

mechanics.name: Inventory and window synchronization
mechanics.note: The server keeps each client's view of its window and sends the slots that differ after a tick, the whole window when the client describes another one or clicked on a stale state id; each window counts its own state ids. As both official servers do, an item use that changes the stack it takes from sends the whole own window (with a chest open, before the chest window's changes), one that leaves its stack as it was sends only what else changed, and a drop's change of the held slot is not sent
